review_locator: PMCID:PMC2965564, From the cradle to the grave: activities of GATA-3 throughout T cell development and differentiation
primary_title: Transcription factor-dependent chromatin remodeling of Il18r1 during Th1 and Th2 differentiation
decision_basis: The review identifies GATA3 as a repressor of the Th1-associated Il18r1 locus; the cited primary demonstrates GATA3 occupancy at conserved non-coding regions and ectopic-GATA3-dependent reduction of Il18r1 mRNA and IL-18Ralpha surface expression.
limitations_preserved: Promote only bounded locus repression in the Th2/Th1 differentiation context. GATA3 binds conserved non-coding regions rather than the promoter in the primary; preserve STAT4/STAT6 and T-cell-state cooperation, and do not infer loss of IL-18 protein function, SCI effects or terminal-TF effects automatically.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC8607625, STAT proteins: a kaleidoscope of canonical and non-canonical functions in immunity and cancer
primary_title: The Transcription Factor STAT6 Mediates Direct Repression of Inflammatory Enhancers and Limits Activation of Alternatively Polarized Macrophages
decision_basis: The review identifies IL-4-activated STAT6 as a transcriptional repressor of inflammatory macrophage enhancers; the cited primary demonstrates STAT6-dependent repression of Il1b transcription, enhancer eRNA and RNA polymerase II activity, with reduced IL-1beta production after IL-4 priming.
limitations_preserved: Promote as IL-4/STAT6-dependent inflammatory gene repression in macrophages. The mechanism involves STAT6-bound enhancer remodeling and context-dependent p65/HDAC/NCoR effects; do not infer universal IL1B repression, absence of inflammasome signaling, SCI effects or terminal-TF effects automatically.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC8607625, STAT proteins: a kaleidoscope of canonical and non-canonical functions in immunity and cancer
primary_title: The Transcription Factor STAT6 Mediates Direct Repression of Inflammatory Enhancers and Limits Activation of Alternatively Polarized Macrophages
decision_basis: The review identifies IL-4/STAT6 as a repressive macrophage-polarization pathway; the cited primary demonstrates IL-4- and STAT6-dependent reduction of Nlrp3 transcription and protein, with reduced inflammasome activation and pyroptosis in alternatively polarized macrophages.
limitations_preserved: Promote only the bounded IL-4/STAT6-dependent Nlrp3 gene-repression branch. Preserve the macrophage polarization and LPS/ATP challenge context and the distinction between reduced Nlrp3 transcription and downstream inflammasome function; do not infer universal repression, SCI effects or terminal-TF effects automatically.
